results.body:
With Clio's AI features, you can gain real-time insight into your firm's performance and personal metrics. You can use the AI Launchpad to query standard reports or use the Custom Reports feature to start building reports using AI-suggested parameters.

Tip: Learn more about generating reports in Clio Manage.

Generate reports

You can query Clio's AI via the Ask a Question chat panel or ask questions directly in Custom Reports. Manage AI will prompt you for any missing information to ensure your report is accurate and complete.

AI Launchpad

  1. Access the AI Launchpad by clicking the gem icon in the main navigation bar.
  2. Select Ask a question.
  3. Ask Manage AI to generate a standard report by providing the report name and time frame.
    • Example query: Generate the productivity by user report for the past month.
    • Example query: Tell me about my firm's revenue performance for the past month.
  4. Click the report link that Clio's AI feature generates to view the full details.

 

Reports

  1. In Clio Manage, go to the main Reports tab, then select the Reports tab.
  2. Ask about your firm's performance with simple questions to build a report with natural language under the Manage AI gem, and click the Send arrow.
  3. Review the relevant fields and calculations pre-selected by Clio's AI.
  4. Optional: Select Columns, Filters, or Groups to re-arrange, filter, or group data.
  5. Optional: Click Edit report settings in the top right to edit your data set and calculations.

 

Monitor personal performance targets

You can query Clio's AI about various personal performance metrics configured in your account settings.

Tip: You can configure your personal performance targets in your account settings.
  1. Access the AI Launchpad by clicking the Manage AI gem.
  2. Select Ask a Question and enter your query.
  3. Enter a personal metric query. Example queries include:
    • Billed/unbilled hours: Show me the total hours billed over the past month.
    • Non-billable hours: Show my non-billable hours for last week.
    • Realization rate: What is my realization rate for the last quarter?
    • Collection rate: What is the percentage of my billed hours that have been successfully billed and collected in the last quarter?
    • Utilization Rate: What percentage of available hours did I spend on billable work in the last 30 days?

results.name: Clio Manage Billing Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Billing Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Billing reports provide a comprehensive overview of accounts receivables, amounts billed, outstanding balances, billable work in progress, billing history, and bill payments and refunds. See below for a summary of each billing report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.
Tip: Learn more about generating reports, creating reports presets, and viewing a history of generated reports here.

Accounts receivable report

The accounts receivable report is designed to help firms determine and quantify billable amounts that are outstanding on all unpaid and past due bills on a per user, per client, and per matter basis. This report details amounts due on approved outstanding bills, partial payments made toward those amounts, accrued interest, and credit notes applied to bills. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Invoice number

This column shows invoice numbers for all bills that are outstanding. If a bill has been approved but is not paid, you will see it listed under this column. If the bill is in draft, it will not appear in this report.

Status

This column shows either Past Due or Open. If a bill is overdue and past its grace period or due date, this column will show the bill as Past Due. If a bill has been approved bit is still within the grace period or due date, this column will show the bill as Open.

Due date

This column lists the due date for the bill or interest charge. If the due date has passed and interest is to be applied as per the payment profile, there will be an additional line in this column showing when the next interest charge is due.

Amount

This column shows the total for each bill, including interest charges. The total does not include payments, credit notes, or taxes. 

Payments

This column shows bill payments and interest charges from direct payments or payments recorded from operating or trust accounts.

Credit notes

This column shows amounts written off on bills.

Balance

This column shows the dollar amount that is outstanding on the bill or interest charge after any payments or credit notes have been applied. This is the amount that still needs to be paid.

Matter total

This total summarizes the amounts that are outstanding for the matter.

Client total

This total summarizes the amounts that are outstanding across all of a client's matters.

Attorney total

This total appears if you sort the report by attorney. It is the total amount summarized for all matters that are assigned to the responsible attorney, including a total for matters not assigned to any responsible attorney.

 

Accounts receivable aging report

The accounts receivable aging report is designed to help firms track unpaid bills. This report groups overdue accounts receivables by the amount of time bills have been past due. You can use this report to follow up with clients whose bills are overdue. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Matter

This column shows matters that have unpaid or overdue bills.

Originating attorney

This column shows the originating attorney assigned to the matter.

Responsible attorney

This column shows the responsible attorney assigned to the matter.

Bill id

This column shows the bill associated with the matter and line items. 

Current

This column shows the amount currently due for an approved bill that is not overdue. Only bills within their grace period will appear in this column.

1-30 days

This column shows overdue amounts that are past 1-30 days of the bill due date.

31-60 days

This column shows overdue amounts that are past 31-60 days of the bill due date.

61-90 days

This column shows overdue amounts that are past 61-90 days of the bill due date.

91+ days

This column shows overdue amounts that are 91 days or more past the bill due date.

Total

This column shows the total amount that is overdue or unpaid.

Matter total

This total summarizes the total amount overdue or unpaid for each of a client's matters.

Client total

This total summarizes the total amount overdue or unpaid for each client.

Attorney total

This total appears if you sort the report by originating or responsible attorney. It is the total amount summarized for all matters that the originating or responsible attorney is assigned.

Total uncategorized

This total appears if you sort the report by originating or responsible attorney and there are matters with no assigned originating or responsible attorney. It is the total amount overdue or unpaid for each matter that does not have an originating or responsible attorney.

 

Billing history report

The billing history report is designed to give firms a detailed view of bills that are unpaid (open), paid, and past due. This report shows bill status, due dates, payments, credit notes, interest, and the balance. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Invoice number

This column shows invoice numbers for all bills that are outstanding, past due, or paid.

Status

This column shows whether a bill it outstanding, past due, or paid. A bill is considered paid when a full payment has been received. Open bills are approved bills that are within their grace period and have not received full payment. Past due bills are outside of their grace period and have not received full payment.

Due date

This column shows the due date for the bill.

Amount

This column shows the total for each bill, including interest charges. 

Payments

This column shows bill payments and interest charges from direct payments or payments recorded from operating or trust accounts.

Credit notes

This column shows amounts written off on bills.

Balance

This column shows the dollar amount that is outstanding on the bill or interest charge after any payments or credit notes have been applied. This is the amount that still needs to be paid.

Matter total

This total summarizes the amounts that are outstanding for the matter.

Client total

This total summarizes the amounts that are outstanding across all of a client's matters.

Attorney total

This total appears if you sort the report by attorney. It is the total amount summarized for all matters that are assigned to the responsible attorney, including a total for matters not assigned to any responsible attorney.

 

Matter balance summary report

The matter balance summary report is designed to give firms a quick view of receivables, current billable work in progress, and expenses in progress across matters. You can also show client and matter trust funds. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Matter

This column shows matters. If you group results by client, all of a client's matters will be listed together. If you group results by attorney, a client's matters may be separated depending on the responsible attorney assigned to the matter.

Accounts receivable

This column shows outstanding time and expense entry amounts on approved, unpaid bills. This is the money that your firm is expecting to receive on open matters. Amounts on a draft bill will not be included in this total.

Work in progress

This column shows unbilled time and expense entries.

Expenses in progress

This column shows amounts for time and expense entires on unbilled bills. It includes entries created and added to bills in draft and bills pending approval. 

Total

This total is the combined total of the accounts receivable, work in progress, and expenses in progress for which your firm expects to receive funds.

Client trust funds

If you chose to show this, it will show client trust funds in the specified date range.

Matter trust funds

If you chose to show this, it will show matter trust funds in the specified date range.

 

Invoice payments report

The invoice payments report is designed to give firms a summary of bill payments and Clio Payments refunds made on bills, the allocation of payments toward each bill line item including overpayments, and the firm users responsible for the line items. This report shows accrued interest, tax, credit notes, and billable time and expenses. You can use this report to calculate staff compensation amounts based on billable work and for listing bill payments for account reconciliation.

Note: By default, partial payments and credit notes applied to invoices are allocated proportionally across all line items. If you change this setting to allocate partial payments and credit notes in a different way, the Credit column and the summary table at the bottom will be calculated depending on the selected allocation method. Learn more about the reports allocation setting here.

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

The first date in this column shows the date that the payment was applied to the bill invoice. The subsequent dates are for each line item on the bill invoice, including service and expense items.

Client

This column shows the name of the client who was billed.

Matter

This column shows the name of the matter that the bill was generated for. Multi-matter bills will show separately and sequentially on the report by matter number.

Transaction

The first item in this column shows the source of the payment applied toward the bill. The subsequent transactions are for each line item the payment was applied to, including services, expenses, and taxes. Next to each line item is the attorney responsible for that service or expense. 

Invoice

This column shows the bill invoice number that the payment was applied to.

Debit

This column shows the payment amount applied to the bill. Overpayments will be listed as separate line items.

Credit

This column shows the charges for line items on bills that have been paid by the payment listed under the Debit column. If a bill is not fully paid, it will only show the line items that the payment was available to be applied to.

Total

This total shows the total amount of Debits followed by the total amount of Credits.

 

Forex gains & losses report

If your firm bills and records payments in multiple currencies, the Forex gains & losses report allows you to see information about your gains and losses resulting from currency conversion. When generated, this report includes the transaction date, client name and matter, invoice number, the amount paid, the conversion rate used at the time the bill was issued, the conversion rate used at the time of payment, the amount gained or lost as a result of the conversion, and the currency totals.

results.title: Clio Manage Online Payments Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Online payments reports provide a comprehensive overview of online payments transactions for firms that have Clio Payments enabled. See below for a summary of each payments report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio uses unique criteria to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about the reports available with your subscription plan and how to upgrade your plan here.
Tip: Learn more about generating reports, creating report presets, and viewing a history of generated reports here.

Monthly statements report

The monthly statements report is designed to give firms using Clio Payments a detailed history of all online payments. You can use this report like a monthly bank statement for bookkeeping and tax purposes.

 

Ledger report

The ledger report is designed to give firms using Clio Payments a detailed view of all transactions by type and status. This report includes charges, fees, refunds, disputes, and payouts, along with transactions that are authorized, completed, failed, disputed, dispute won, dispute lost, voided, and refunded. You can use this report to reconcile records between bank accounts and transactions in Clio.

 

Transaction report

The transaction report is designed to give firms using Clio Payments a detailed view of authorized payment transactions, including charges and processing fees.

 

Deposit report

The deposit report provides firms using Clio Payments with a detailed breakdown of deposit amounts and the corresponding transaction fees. This report does not show authorized payments. You can use this report to identify total fees charged daily and monthly, and view the net amount deposited. This report is the most effective tool for tracking transactions that show a Complete status but have not yet appeared in your bank account. To track a payment deposit:

  1. Click Reports and select Clio Payments.
  2. Click Deposit Report.
  3. Select the date range and bank account, then look for the Payout Date for your specific transaction.

Tip: Identifying the Payout date ensures your firm accounts for the delay between a client's payment and the actual availability of funds, helping you maintain accurate ledger balances.

 

Form 1099-K report

This report provides your firm with a detailed overview of online transactions and settlements processed through Clio Payments. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) requires this report for bank accounts meeting the following annual criteria and a minimum of 200 transactions:

  • 2024: More than $5,000 in total payments.
  • 2025: More than $20,000 in total payments.
  • 2026: More than $20,000 in total payments.

This amount refers to gross amounts and does not include refunds, voided transactions, or adjustments. You can use this report when preparing your taxes.

When you enable Clio Payments, your firm will automatically receive electronic copies of your Form 1099-K report. You can request a paper copy by contacting our payment operations team at payments@clio.com before January 10.

Important: Certain US states, including Missouri, Illinois, Massachusetts, Maryland, Mississippi, Virginia, and Vermont, have lower payment thresholds for this report. Please verify the requirement with your tax authority.

results.name: Clio Manage Personal Injury Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Personal Injury Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insight into how your firm is performing. Clio Manage personal injury reports provide a comprehensive overview of damages, medical expenses, and medical expense payments across your firm's personal injury matters. See below for a summary of each personal injury report in Clio Manage and the type of information these reports offer.

Note: Personal injury reports are a component of Clio's Personal Injury Add-On and are not available for all Clio subscription plans. See which plans have Clio's Personal Injury Add-On here. If you have questions about upgrading, contact Clio's support or sales teams here. 

Tip: Learn more about generating the damages report here and the medical expense and medical expense payments reports here.

Damages report

The damages report is designed to give firms an overview of medical bills and damages recorded on a matter. This report separates the medical bill summary from the list of all other damages manually recorded in the Damages subtab. The medical bill summary shows medical bill information such as paid amounts, adjustments, owed amounts, and bill amounts. The damages section below shows damages by type, a description of damages, the amount of each damage. You can use this report to track all damages and medical bill amounts for a personal injury matter. 

Note: This report is only available in CSV format.

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

  • Type: This shows the type of damage, with options for special general, and other damage types.
  • Description: This shows the description of each damage.
  • Amount: This shows the amount of each special, general, or other damage.
  • Bill amount: This is specific to the medical bill summary. It is a summary of all medical bill amounts recorded in the Medical records subtab.
  • Adjustment: This is specific to the medical bill summary. It is a summary of all adjustments on medical bills recorded in the Medical records subtab.
  • Total paid: This is specific to the medical bill summary. It is a summary of all amounts paid on medical bills recorded in the Medical records subtab.
  • Balance owed: This is specific to the medical bill summary. It is a summary of all outstanding balances on medical bills recorded in the Medical records subtab.
  • Paid + owed: This is specific to the medical bill summary. It is a summary of all medical bill payments, plus the outstanding balances owed to medical providers, as recorded in the Medical records subtab.

 

Medical expenses report

The medical expenses report is designed to give firms an overview of medical expenses recorded on a matter. This report shows medical expenses by medical provider, including medical bills, adjustments, liens, and outstanding balances. You can use this report to track all medical expenses for a personal injury matter. 

Note: This report is only available in CSV format.

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

  • Matter: This shows the matter associated with the generated report.
  • Client: This shows the contact associated with the matter.
  • Responsible attorney: This shows the firm user responsible for the matter. You can change this field by editing the matter.
  • Total billed by all medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount billed by all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Bill amount column for all medical bills added to the matter. 
  • Total paid to all medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount paid to all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Total paid column for all medical bills added to the matter.
  • Total adjustments by medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount of medical bill adjustments recorded for all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Adjustment column for all medical bills added to the matter.
  • Total balance due to all medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount that is owed to all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Balanced owed column for all medical bills added to the matter.
  • Summary report: This section of the report shows the treatment date and medical bill details entered for each medical provider for the matter. This section includes the medical provider's name and description, the dates that the client was first treated and then last treated, and the amounts billed, paid, adjusted, and due for each added medical bill.
  • Detailed report: This section of the report shows the medical bill details entered for each medical provider that has at least one attached medical bill. This section includes the medical provider's name, the bill's date and amount, each payer's name, amount paid, and whether the amount was marked as a lien or outstanding balance, the total paid by all payers, any recorded adjustments, any balances owed to the medical provider, and whether the balance owed to the medical provider was marked as a lien or outstanding balance. 

 

Medical expense payments report

The medical expenses report is designed to give firms an overview of medical expense payments recorded on a matter. This report shows medical expense payments by payer, including medical providers associated with the medical bills, medical bill payments, liens, and outstanding balances. You can use this report to track all medical expense payments made to payers for a personal injury matter. 

Note: This report is only available in CSV format.

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

  • Matter: This shows the matter associated with the generated report.
  • Client: This shows the contact associated with the matter.
  • Responsible attorney: This shows the firm user responsible for the matter. You can change this field by editing the matter.
  • Total billed by all medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount billed by all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Bill amount column for all medical bills added to the matter. 
  • Total paid to all medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount paid to all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Total paid column for all medical bills added to the matter.
  • Total adjustments by medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount of medical bill adjustments recorded for all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Adjustment column for all medical bills added to the matter.
  • Total balance due to all medical providers: This shows the total dollar amount that is owed to all medical providers for the matter. This number is a cumulation of the values under the Balanced owed column for all medical bills added to the matter.
  • Summary report: This section of the report shows the amount paid to each payer, whether the amount was marked as a lien or outstanding balance, and the lien or outstanding balance amount. 
  • Detailed report: This section of the report shows medical bill details for each payer on each bill. This section includes the medical provider associated with the medical bill, the bill's date and amount, the amount that was paid to the listed payer, and whether the amount paid to the payer was marked as a lien or outstanding balance.

results.name: Reports Permissions and Settings
results.title: Reports Permissions and Settings
results.body:
Access to reports in both Clio Grow and Clio Manage requires specific permissions on your user profile. Clio Manage users require reports permissions, and Clio Grow users require admin permissions to view reports. Additionally, Clio Manage administrators can change the payment allocation setting to determine how partial payments should be applied to certain reports.

Note: Only administrators can perform the actions listed in this article.

Change reports permissions in Clio Grow

In Clio Grow, a user can either have admin or normal permissions. Only users with admin permissions can view reports and provide access to other users to view reports. If you are an administrator, follow the steps below to give another firm user reports permissions.

Important: All users with admin permissions can view reports, export contacts and matters to CSV, invite users, deactivate users, add or remove licenses, and update firm billing information.
  1. Go to Settings > Account.
  2. In the User settings section, select a user’s Normal permission.
  3. Select Admin and then click Assign permission.

 

Change reports permissions in Clio Manage

In Clio Manage, users need reports permissions to view and generate reports. Once a user has reports permissions, they can view all reports in Clio Manage. You cannot restrict reports. If you are an administrator, follow the steps below to give another firm user report permissions.

Important: Granting a user reports permissions will give them access to other firm users’ productivity, including activities and billing rates, when viewing reports even if the user does not have billing permissions.
For one user For multiple users in bulk
  1. Go to Settings > Manage Users.
  2. Click Edit below the user’s name.
  3. Scroll down to Permissions.
  4. Check the box for Reports.
  5. Click Save New Information.
  1. Go to Settings > Groups, Permissions, and Job Titles > Permissions.
  2. Scroll down to Reports.
  3. Check or uncheck the boxes next to users’ names.

 

Change reports allocation setting in Clio Manage

Clio Manage reports help you quickly gauge how much of your client payments come from different line item categories. By default, partial payments and credit notes are applied to all line items proportionally. Administrators can also choose a different payment allocation method for how partial payments and credit notes are applied to line items in specific reports. Once a new method is selected, only reports generated after choosing the new method will be affected.

Note: This setting will affect the following reports: invoice payments report, fee allocation report, revenue report, and the originating attorney revenue report. This setting will also affect the collection rate in your Firm Dashboard.

  1. Go to Settings > Billing.
  2. Select Reports allocation.
  3. Under Payment allocation, select the allocation method of your choice. There are four allocation methods to choose from. See below for an explanation of each and a table with examples of how a partial payment would be allocated across report line items depending on the selected method.
    • Option 1: Pay all line items proportionally
    • Option 2: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services oldest to newest
    • Option 3: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services proportionally
    • Option 4: Pay services oldest to newest first and then expenses oldest to newest
  4. Click Save setting.

 

Allocation method explanation:

Option 1: Pay all line items proportionally

  • This is the default setting. A partial payment will be applied to line items based on each line item's percentage of the total bill cost. For example, a $400 expense on a $1000 invoice is 40% of the invoice. If that invoice receives a payment of $800, 40% of that partial payment amount is $320, so the expense will receive a $320 payment.
  • This method is also used by accounting systems like QuickBooks Online (QBO) and Xero. Use this method if you want your firm's reporting data in Clio Manage to match the reporting data in QBO or Xero. 

Option 2: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services oldest to newest

  • A partial payment will be first applied to expense line items from the oldest dated to newest dated, followed by services (time entries) from oldest dated to newest. If the payment is fully used before all line items are paid, the remaining line items will show $0 in reports.
  • If you use reports to determine how to pay employees based on their recorded time, you may want to use the option 3 (pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services proportionally) since option 2 will result in employees who did work earlier on the invoice being compensated first.

Option 3: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services proportionally

  • A partial payment will be first applied to expense line items from the oldest dated to newest dated. Services (time entries) will then be paid proportionally based on each service's percentage of the total of all services on the invoice, NOT the invoice total. This method can help pay all employees who did work on the invoice equally.
  • For example, if, after paying all expenses, there is $100 of a partial payment remaining and a total of $300 in services, with service 1 for $200 (two-thirds of the total service amount) and service 2 for $100 (one-third of the total service amount), service 1 will receive $66.67 and service 2 will receive $33.33. 

Option 4: Pay services oldest to newest first and then expenses oldest to newest

  • If you select this option, a partial payment will be first applied to service line items from the oldest dated to newest dated, followed by expense line items from oldest dated to newest. If the payment is fully used before all line items are paid, the remaining line items will show $0 in reports.

 

Example:

In this example, you sent your client a $1000 invoice with two expense line items and two service line items. Your client paid a partial payment of $800 toward the invoice. When you generate a report containing invoice line items, the four line items will be allocated the paid $800 depending on the allocation setting you chose. The table below shows how much of the payment would go toward each line item depending on each allocation method option.

 

Set allocations in Clio Manage

The fee allocation report is designed give your firm a detailed view of the time and expenses each user has billed and collected for each matter. To help you easily determine your firm's compensation and bonus structures, administrators can also set how much of the collected time in the fee allocation report should be allocated to originating attorney, responsible attorneys, and responsible staff. Previously generated reports will not be affected by updated attorney allocations.

Note: This is a firm-wide setting that will affect all fee allocation reports. Firm administrators can also override the firm-wide setting for any individual matter by changing the allocation percentages for that matter.

  1. Go to Settings > Billing.
  2. Select Reports allocation.
  3. Under Fee allocation, enter percentage allocations for the different firm members.
  4. Click Save setting.

results.name: Clio Manage Matter Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Matter Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Matter reports provide a comprehensive overview of matter listings, matters by responsible attorney, contact listing, and billing rate. See below for a summary of each matter report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.
Tip: Learn more about generating reports, creating reports presets, and viewing a history of generated reports here.

Matters report

The matters report is designed to give firms a detailed view of clients and matters. This report includes matter description, responsible attorney, originating attorney, last bill date, accounts receivable, whether the matter is billable, practice area, status of the matter, and the client’s name. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists the name of the client attached to the matter and is sorted alphabetically by client last name.

Matter

This column lists each of a client's matters.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field when a matter was created.

Practice area

This column shows the practice area for the matter. If a practice area was not selected, this column will be blank.

Status

This column shows the matter's current status. A matter can either be Open, Pending, or Closed. 

Responsible attorney

This column shows the firm user currently responsible for the matter.

Originating attorney

This column shows the firm user that was selected as the originating attorney on the matter.

Billable

This column shows whether the matter is billable or non-billable.

Accounts receivable

This column shows the amount currently owed on an outstanding bill. This column will only show approved bills that have not been paid.

Latest bill

This column shows the date that the last bill was generated.

 

Matters by responsible attorney report

The matters by responsible attorney report is designed to give firms a quick view of matters grouped by responsible attorney. This report includes the client’s name and matter description. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Matter

This column lists each of a client's matters.

Client

This column lists the name of the client attached to the matter. If a client was deleted or reassigned from a matter, you will see a blank space under this column. Clients are sorted alphabetically by client last name for each responsible attorney.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field when a matter was created.

No assigned responsible attorney

This section appears below all of the matters with responsible attorneys and shows matters and clients that do not have an assigned responsible attorney.

 

Contact information report

The contact information report is designed to give firms a quick view of clients, their matters, and basic contact information. You can use this report to generate an email list. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client name

This column lists the name of the client attached to a matter. If a client has more than one matter, you will see their name listed again for each matter.

Matter

This column lists each of a client's matters.

Primary phone number

This column shows the client's first phone number or the phone number that is designated as the primary phone number.

Primary email address

This column shows the client's first email address or the email address that is designated as the primary email address.

 

Billing rate report

The billing rate report is designed to give firms an overview of custom billing rates for all matters. It shows matters, users, and the current client, matter, and user default billing rates. This report helps you identify which clients, staff, or practice areas bring in the most revenue and provides insight into the accuracy and effectiveness of your firm's billing rates. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists clients with matters that have time and expense entries on file and is sorted alphabetically by client first name. Clients with multiple matters will appear multiple times.

Matter number

This column lists each of a client's matters and shows the matter number.

Matter description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field when a matter was created.

User

This column shows the name of the firm user whose billing rate is applied to the matter. 

Practice area

This column shows the practice area selected when the matter was created. If no practice area was selected, this column will be blank.

Rate type

This column shows the rate type that you selected before generating the report. Selecting Default and custom rates will show user, client, and matter rates. Selecting Custom matter rates only will show only matter rates. Selecting Custom client rates only will show only client rates. Selecting Custom matter and client rates only will show the matter and client rates, but not the user's default rate.

Each client row in the export will show the billing rate that the matter is using and is contingent on rate hierarchy. The rate hierarchy is as follows: User Matter Rate > User Client Rate > User Default Rate. This means that a custom billing rate set on the matter will always override custom rates on the contact and the user's default rate set in their profile. Learn more about rate hierarchy here.

User's matter rate

This column lists the custom billing rate added to the matter. This rate can be changed by editing the matter and going to the Billing preference section. If there is no custom matter rate, this column will be blank.

User's client rate

This column lists the custom billing rate added to the client's file. This rate can be changed by editing the contact and going to the Billing preference section. If there is no custom client rate, this column will be blank.

User's default rate

This column shows the default billing rate for the user who created the matter. This rate can be changed in Settings > Profile.

Matter open date

This column shows the date that the matter was opened.

Originating attorney

This column shows the firm user selected as the originating attorney on the matter.

Responsible attorney

This column shows the firm user selected as the responsible attorney on the matter.

results.name: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Client reports provide a comprehensive overview of client balances, bank account and matter transaction history, non-billable and billable work in progress, and trust account balances. On matters with multiple clients, most reports apply to the default client only. The Matter balance summary, Trust management, Invoice payments, Client Ledger, and Trust Listing reports support multiple clients on a matter.

See below for a summary of each client report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.

Client activity report

The client activity report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of billed and unbilled time and expense activities across matters. This report does not include non-billable time. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

Activity type

This column shows whether the recorded activity is a time entry or expense entry.

Status

This column shows whether the activities are billed or unbilled. Activities are divided by billed and unbilled status, with billed activities appearing first with their subtotal, followed by unbilled activities.

User

This column lists the firm user who created the activity entry.

Activity category

This column shows the activity category recorded when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Description

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses for the listed activity.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for the matter.

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for each of a client's matters.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for all of a client's matters.

 

Client ledger report

The client ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed view of client trust and operating transactions. This report also shows payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust ledger report

The trust ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of client and matter transactions and balances across all trust accounts. The report includes payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. You can use this report to submit to regulators. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Payer/Payee

This column shows information about the person making or receiving a payment. This information is useful when the payer or payee is not the client themselves.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust interest calculation report

The trust interest calculation report is designed to calculate interest earned on deposited client matter trust funds across all trust accounts. You can use this report to calculate interest for trust funds based on rate, compounding period, and date range for a specific client or matter. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the IOLTA account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists trust funds deposited into the IOLTA account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money remaining after each listed transaction.

Rate

This column lists the selected interest rate for each deposit.

Balance start date

The start date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Balance end date

The end date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Days held

This column shows the total number of days of the interest period you selected to generate the report.

Interest

This column shows the amount of interest accrued based on the balance for the selected period.

A summary of the Closing balance, Total interest, and Closing balance with interest is also provided for each calculation in the report.

If you generate this report in Clio, i.e., you generate a Web report, you have the option to post the calculated interest directly to the client funds you hold. Next to the Total interest amount calculated for the client funds held in a client funds account (per matter and client), click Apply Interest. You can change the transaction date and description for the transaction, then click Record transaction to create this ledger entry in the client funds account. The Source/Destination field for the entry will be “Trust Interest Calculation Report”.

Once you apply interest to the client funds, your subsequent Client funds interest reports will show the last five transactions where you applied interest to the account.

 

Trust management report

The trust management report is designed to give firms an overview of unbilled time and expense activities, trust account balances, and minimum trust thresholds. You can use this report to compare billable work against trust fund holdings. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists the name of each client

Matter

This column lists the matters for each client.

Unbilled amount

This column shows the amount of unbilled time and expense entries for each matter.

Amount in trust

This column shows the amount of funds currently in trust for the client or matter.

Minimum threshold

This column lists the minimum threshold set for matter trust funds. This amount can be changed by editing the matter and changing the number for Trust balance notification under Billing preference.

Amount below minimum

This column shows the amount that a trust balance has fallen below the minimum threshold set for the matter.

 

 

Trust listing report

The trust listing report is designed to give firms a quick summary of client trust fund balances across all client accounts. This report includes an opening and closing balance summary. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Account name

This column shows the name of the trust account.

Last activity date

This column shows the most recent transaction in the client's trust account.

Client balance

This column shows the current amount in trust for the client. This balance may be different from the amount shown in the matter's Dashboard if you generate the report for a specific date range. This means that if a client had trust funds in the account before that selected date range and payments were made during the date range, the report will only pull in transactions, which will result in a negative balance.

Unlinked

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Include balances not associated with a client before running the report. It shows trust funds that are not linked to a specific client.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Work in progress report

The work in progress report is designed to give firms a detailed view of unbilled time and expense activities for matters. This report only shows activities on bills in draft, bills pending approval, and activities not on any bills. It will not show activities on any approved or paid bills. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

User

This column lists the firm user assigned on the activity entry.

Description

This column shows the activity category selected when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Note

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for each of the client's matters.

Client total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for all of the client's matters.

 

Bank account activity report

The bank account activity report is designed to give firms a detailed view of funds in and funds out across all firm bank accounts. This report also includes the account balance. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Client

This column lists the client associated with the transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered into the Description field when a payment was recorded.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

There are three different dashboards and an organization timeline to help you keep track of how time is spent on matters and grants:

Personal Dashboard:

This dashboard shows a high-level overview of your agenda, how you are spending your time, and financial metrics. A comprehensive description of the dashboard is provided here. When grant information is tracked it also includes information about how you are spending your time in relation to grants and their associated matters.

  • Time allocation: This section shows your time entries in hours for the specified timeframe. If grants are associated with any time entries, they are listed in this section.
    • You can use the Filter to display information about the proportion of time allocated to each grant in hours, as a percentage, or both.
    • You can click Review activities for any listed grant to view a table of the transactions associated with that grant.
    • You can select a date range and relevant filters to view specific information and export the data using Export CSV.

Organization Dashboard:

Note: The primary subscriber or users with administrator permissions can view this dashboard.

This dashboard shows a high-level overview of how firm members are spending their time and what their billing practices are. A comprehensive description of the dashboard is provided here. When grant information is tracked, it also includes information about how firm members are spending their time in relation to grants and on matters associated with grants.

  • Time allocation: This section shows time entries for the specified timeframe across firm users.
    • You can use the Filter to display information about the proportion of time allocated to each grant in hours, as a percentage, or both.
    • You can click Review activities for any listed grant to view a table of the transactions associated with that grant.
    • You can select a date range and relevant filters to view specific information and export the data using Export CSV.

Organization Feed:

This feed shows a timeline of all organization-wide activity in the account. A comprehensive description of the feed is provided here. Relevant to grants, the feed provides information related to grant spend down via salaries, such as updates to grant allocations, changes to salary amounts, and the spend down amounts.

Matter Dashboard:

This dashboard provides an overview of matter information. A comprehensive description of the feed is provided here. When you add a grant to a matter, that matter's dashboard will show a new section for grants associated with the matter.

 

Generate a matters and grants report

If you use grants at your firm, you can generate a Matters & grants report which offers information similar to a matter report but with additional options to filter by grant, matter custom fields, and client custom fields.

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. In the list of categories, select Matters.
  3. Click Matters & grants.
  4. Make your selections.
  5. Click Generate report.

 

Export matters with associated grants

In the main Matters tab, you can select columns and specify filters relevant to a particular export you may need to track a specific deliverable, including cases closed under a specific grant. When adding a grant to a matter, if you check the box for Use this grant for case reporting, the grant will appear in the Grants column and in the export.

Tip: When selecting your filters and columns, you also have the option to select custom fields. These custom fields will appear in your export, allowing you to report on them.

  1. Go to Matters.
  2. Click Columns, check the box for Grants, and then click Update columns.
  3. Select Filters to sort data by specific filters, including specific grants or custom fields, and then click Apply filters.
  4. Optional: In the search box, use a keyword search to filter your matters.
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.

 

Export activities with associated grants

In the main Activities tab, you can select columns and specify filters relevant to a particular export you may need to track a specific deliverable. To export grant information from the Activities tab:

  1. Go to Activities.
  2. Click Columns, check the boxes for Grant and Matter, and then click Update columns.
  3. Select Filters to sort data by specific filters, including specific grants, and then click Apply filters.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.

 

Export grants

In the Grants tab, you can export your organization's grants to get an understanding of how much of a spend down there has been from the grants. The data will be exported in CSV format.

  1. Go to Grants.
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.
Note: All active and archived grants will be exported regardless of the subtab you selected.

 

Export grant transactions

You can export the transactions associated with a grant to get an understanding of the detailed financials of a specific grant. The data will be exported in CSV format and will show grant spend down in your firm.

  1. Go to Grants.
  2. Select the name of a grant to view its transactions.

  3. Optional: You can add or remove columns to include or exclude in the export by clicking Columns, selecting and/or deselecting column fields, and clicking Update columns.

    Note: You can select a time period to filter the list of transactions in the table, but the export will include all transactions for a grant regardless of the time period you selected.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.
  5. Choose between exporting Available columns, which will include all available columns even if you previously deselected them, or Visible columns only to include only those columns you appearing in the table view.
  6. Click Export.

results.name: Clio Scheduler
results.title: Clio Scheduler
results.body:
Clio Scheduler is an online appointment booking tool for prospective clients. Prospective clients can book appointments in available time slots and pay for appointments in advance if your firm has Clio Payments enabled. Once booked, appointments will appear in your Clio Manage calendar according to your settings configured for event sharing between Clio Grow and Clio Manage. When configuring your Clio Scheduler settings, you can set up your firm booking page to host multiple appointment types across your firm and customize how Clio Scheduler is displayed.

Note: All settings and appointment setups are done in Clio Grow.

 

Create appointment types

In Clio Grow, appointment types are templates of appointments that you commonly schedule with prospective clients. You can add appointment types to Clio Scheduler to allow prospective clients to book appointments themselves. Once a prospective client books an unpaid appointment, it will be added to your Lead inbox. Paid appointments will be added to your Pipeline.

Tip: Once the appointment type is created, click the appointment link URL to view what your prospective clients will see.

  1. Go to Settings > Calendar & appointments.
  2. Under the My appointment types section, click New appointment type.
  3. See the accordion sections below to learn more about each section in the appointment type creation tool.
Appointment information
  1. Enter basic information for your appointment type, including the appointment type's name and description. 
    • The location and internal note are not visible to prospective clients.
  2. Optional: Check the box for Make this a Zoom meeting. Learn more about Zoom in Clio Grow.
  3. Optional: Check the box for Add this appointment type to firm booking page. Learn more about the firm booking page below.
  4. Click Save and close.
Basic booking details
  1. Complete basic booking settings.
    • Duration: Select how long this appointment type will be.
    • Recurring availability: Select which days and times are available for prospective clients to book for this appointment type.
  2. Click Save and close.
Advanced booking settings
  1. Set advanced booking details.
    • Start time increments: Select how often appointments can be started each hour.
    • Minimum advance booking: Set the minimum amount of time required between the time of a booking and the start of an appointment. This setting can prevent a prospective client from booking the day of the appointment.
    • Buffer before appointment: Set a buffer before the appointment type to avoid back-to-back appointments.
    • Buffer after appointment: Set a buffer after the appointment type to avoid back-to-back appointments.
  2. Click Save and close.

Note: Buffers are not displayed on your Clio Manage calendar.

Emails

When your prospective client books an appointment via the Clio Scheduler booking link, you can choose which emails they receive for appointment invitation, confirmation, and reminder. You can also create multiple email templates for each. Learn more about creating email templates here.

  1. Under Invitation email, select the email template that will be sent once a prospective client books an appointment via the Clio Scheduler booking link.
    • Under Current email template, select the appropriate email template.
    • Optional: Click View templates to see a preview of the listed templates.
  2. Under Confirmation email, select the email that will be sent to confirm the prospective client's appointment.
    • Under Current email template, select the appropriate email template.
    • Optional: Click View templates to see a preview of the listed templates.
  3. Under Reminder email, select the email that will be sent to remind the prospective client of their upcoming appointment.
    • Under Current email template, select the appropriate email template.
    • Optional: Click View templates to see a preview of the listed templates.
  4. Click Save and close.
Collect payments

If you have Clio Payments enabled on your Clio Manage account, you can accept debit or credit card payments or Apple Pay or Google Pay at the time that a prospective client books an appointment using the Clio Scheduler booking link. Paid appointments will automatically be added to your matter Pipeline.

The payment will either be recorded as a completed transaction in Clio Manage or kept as a credit for the contact for future billing, depending on the selected setting. If the payment is recorded as a transaction, you can find it in the contact’s Transactions subtab.

Note: You can only collect payments if you have Clio Payments enabled, are located in North America, and have at least one of the following permissions: administrator, accounts, or billing.

  1. Check the box for Collect payments for this appointment if you want clients to always pay for this appointment type when booking their appointments.
    • Matter status applied to these new leads: Select the matter status that will be applied to any new leads that book and pay for this appointment type.
    • Amount: Enter the amount due for this appointment type.
    • Linked bank account: Select the bank account that the collected payment funds will be deposited into.
    • When do you want to record the payment as fees earned: Select whether the payment should deposit into your bank account as a transaction or be kept as a credit on the contact’s record for future billing. If you select a trust account as the bank account, you only have the option to keep the payment as a credit for future billing.
  2. Click Create.

 

Edit appointment types

You can change any setting that you initially set when you created an appointment type, including the date and times that you are available for appointments, minimum advanced booking times, start time increments, buffer times, and more.

  1. Go to Settings > Calendar & appointments.
  2. In the section My appointment types, click Edit appointment type for the appointment you want to edit.
  3. Open the appropriate section and make your changes.
  4. Click Save and close.

 

Delete appointment types

  1. Go to Settings > Calendar & appointments.
  2. In the section My appointment types, click Delete for the appointment you want to delete.
  3. When the warning prompt appears, click Delete appointment.

 

Share appointment booking link

When setting up appointments, you can embed a public link on your website that prospective clients can click to schedule appointments. You can also share this link directly with prospective clients.

Tip: You can also add your Clio Scheduler link to your Google Business Profile in Google. Learn more here.

  1. Go to Settings > Calendar & appointments.
  2. In the My appointment types section, click Copy link below the relevant appointment type.
  3. Paste the link on your website or send it to a client by email.

 

Add appointments to firm booking page

With the firm booking page, you can display multiple firm appointment types on a single web page using one link. When a client clicks the firm booking page link, they will see all available appointment types for your firm that you added to the firm booking page. Follow the steps below to add appointment types to the firm booking page.

Note: Only administrators can view this section.

  1. Go to Settings > Calendar & appointments.
  2. In the section Firm booking page click Select appointment types.
  3. Use the checkboxes to select which appointment types you want prospective clients to see.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Copy link to add the link to your website.

 

Customize Scheduler appearance

With Clio Scheduler, you can customize the display name that prospective clients see when booking appointments. If you do not select a display name, the booking page will show your Clio Grow username.

Note: The display name limit is 255 characters.
  1. Go to Settings > Calendar & appointments.

  2. In the My appointment types section, click Edit display name.

    Note: If you did not yet set a display name, click Set display name.
  3. Add or change the name and click Save display name.

 

Pause appointment types

Appointment time slots are always available unless you temporarily pause them by unchecking all available days for all appointment types. When you’re ready to accept appointments again, just re-add days and times. An alternative to pausing appointment types is creating an all-day event in your Clio Manage calendar. When you do this, Clio Scheduler prevents appointments from being booked on the day of the all-day event.

Uncheck available days Create all-day event
  1. Go to Settings > Calendar & appointments.
  2. In the My appointment types section, click Edit appointment type for the appointment type you want to pause.
  3. Expand the Appointment information section.
  4. Uncheck the box Add this appointment type to your Firm Booking page.
  5. Click Save and close.
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Click New event.
  3. Set the start time for the event as 12:00AM and end time as 12:00AM on the last day of your absence.
  4. Complete the remaining details.
  5. Click Save event.

Important: When changing the start and end times, do not select the All Day checkbox. Selecting this checkbox will not affect the appointment type's availability.

 

Cancel booked appointments

When you cancel an appointment, both you and the prospective client will receive an email confirmation. If you need to reschedule or cancel an appointment that your client booked through Clio Scheduler, follow the directions below.

  1. Go to the matter.
  2. Under Intake process, find the appointment booking.
  3. Click the Options dropdown and select Cancel Appointment.
  4. When the warning prompt appears, select Cancel Appointment.

 

Actions for prospective clients

Prospective clients can book appointments by clicking the link you send them or by clicking the Scheduler link embedded in your website. When your prospective client clicks the link, they will be taken to the Scheduler where they can book their appointment, and if required, enter payment information. If an appointment type requires a payment but the prospective client does not provide payment, the appointment will automatically be unscheduled. When the appointment is booked, both you and the prospective client will receive a confirmation email.

When clients book appointments, the default time zone is based on the computer or phone time of the person viewing the scheduler. Your clients can change the time zone when booking appointments upon clicking the appointment link.

Prospective clients can also reschedule and cancel appointments that they booked. The prospective client can reschedule or cancel their booked appointment from the confirmation email by clicking either Reschedule or Cancel. When a prospective client reschedules or cancels an appointment, both you and the prospective client will receive an email notification of the change. Appointment emails are sent from notifications@grow.clio.com. You cannot change this to your firm email.

Important: Only clients can reschedule appointments that they booked. You can only reschedule the appointment if you booked it on behalf of your client. If you need to reschedule an appointment that your client booked, cancel the appointment and create a new one.

results.name: Schedule Events From Documents Using Clio's AI Features
results.title: Schedule Events From Documents Using Clio's AI Features
results.body:
When you upload files like court notices, scheduling orders, and even handwritten meeting notes, you can use Clio's AI features to extract key dates and events from these files and create events in Clio for you to review.

 

Start scheduling events from documents

You can initiate the AI Scheduling process from four main entry points. Clio's AI features use a proactive detection and classification layer to identify when a recently uploaded document contains actionable dates and determines its specific legal purpose.

  • AI Launchpad: Click the AI diamond icon, then click Schedule in the Schedule events from documents card.
  • Matter Dashboard (AI Actions): Clio's AI features proactively identify recently uploaded documents that contain deadlines. Look for suggestions under the AI Actions card from a matter's dashboard. 
  • Personal Dashboard: Go to your home page in Clio Manage (Dashboard > Personal Dashboard) to view high-priority matters where Clio's AI has identified events ready for review. 
  • Calendar: Click the down arrow next to New events and select Extract from a document.

 

Extract and schedule events

When you upload a document, Clio's AI features analyze the content to classify the document type. This classification allows the AI to apply the correct logic for extracting dates specific to that document's legal context.

Note: Clio's AI can analyze a wide variety of documents, including court notices, scheduling orders, and handwritten meeting notes, to extract deadlines and events.

Important: AI Scheduling does not currently apply local court rules for counting days when calculating dates. Always check calculated deadlines against official court rules.

  1. Initiate the scheduling process from one of the entry points listed above.
  2. Under Extract from a document, select an open matter. 
  3. Select the document type. Confirming the document type ensures the AI uses the most accurate classification logic for that specific file.
  4. Select a document or upload a new one. Manage AI can extract events from one document at a time.
    • PDF: up to 20 pages or 10MB
    • Documents: up to 20 pages or 10MB
  5. Click Extract events. Manage AI will extract events in the background.
    • You can wait on the page or, if the process takes a while, you can wait to receive an email notification that the draft events are ready for review. To open the list of events from your email, click Review events.
  6. Review the created events.
    1. Hover over an event to see which part of your document was used to create the event and its details.
    2. Events tagged as Calculated indicate that the event date was calculated relative to another event’s date.
  7. Optional: Click the pencil icon to edit the event details, or click the X icon to remove events that are not needed.
  8. Optional: Click + at the top of the list to add an additional event.
  9. Optional: Click your name (your personal calendar) at the top of the list to select a different calendar or to add the events to the firm’s calendar in addition to the selected calendar.
  10. Click Create events.
    • If you use Automated reminders for the extracted events, you have the opportunity to review and adjust any reminders that were automatically added.
      • Use the pencil icon to edit reminders, or use the trash can icon to delete reminders that were automatically applied to extracted events.
      • Click Add reminders to create additional reminders.
  11. Click Add to calendar when you have reviewed and modified these reminders.
    • Clio's AI will upload all confirmed events to your Clio Calendar simultaneously, creating them in a single batch.

 

Use AI to schedule reminders

You can set up automated scheduling reminders so that Clio's AI can intelligently identify which reminders may need to be added to the event the AI has extracted from documents.

 

Enable/disable automated scheduling reminders

  1. Click Calendar.
  2. Click More > Calendar settings.
  3. Select the Manage AI Scheduling Reminders subtab.
  4. Use the toggle to enable or disable scheduling reminders.

 

Create and manage automated scheduling reminders

Create Edit Duplicate Delete

Clio's AI-driven automated scheduling reminders feature comes preset with recommended reminder workflows that may be useful to your firm. You can also create your own workflow.

  1. Click Calendar.
  2. Click More > Calendar settings.
  3. Select the Manage AI Scheduling Reminders subtab.
  4. Click + Create reminder rules.
  5. Fill the fields to create the automated reminder.
    1. Select the event type condition. You can select from Clio’s list of provided event types, or create your own.
    2. Select who to notify and the notification method. Click Add person to notify more than one person.
    3. Set how long before the event you want the reminder sent. Click + Add time to set more than one reminder.
  6. Click Add reminder workflow.

Your workflow will be added to your list of reminders.

  1. Click Calendar.
  2. Click More > Calendar settings.
  3. Select the Manage AI Scheduling Reminders subtab.
  4. For an existing workflow, click the more icon (vertical ellipses) in the Action column, then select Edit.
  5. Modify the fields as needed.
  6. Click Update reminder workflow.
  1. Click Calendar.
  2. Click More > Calendar settings.
  3. Select the Manage AI Scheduling Reminders subtab.
  4. For an existing workflow, click the more icon (vertical ellipses) in the Action column, then select Duplicate.
  5. Update the fields as needed, then click Add reminder rule.
  1. Click Calendar.
  2. Click More > Calendar settings.
  3. Select the Manage AI Scheduling Reminders subtab.
  4. For an existing workflow, click the more icon (vertical ellipses) in the Action column, then select Remove.
  5. Click OK to confirm the removal.
